context.heading: Deceivers who wandered from the path
context.body: Planos ("deceiver") comes from a verb for leading someone off the road; the related word planētēs gave us "planet," a "wandering" star. These teachers moved from church to church, relying on believers' hospitality. They denied that Jesus Christ came in the flesh, the same error John confronts in 1 John 4:2–3.

context.heading: The teachers who ran ahead
context.body: The false teacher "runs ahead" (proagō, to go before or beyond) without remaining in Christ's teaching. They probably presented themselves as advanced, having moved past the simple apostolic message. John's verdict is blunt: going beyond Christ means leaving God behind.

context.heading: Why the front door mattered
context.body: Churches met in homes, and there were few respectable inns, so welcoming a traveling teacher meant lodging, meals and often a platform before the gathered church. John forbids this for those who deny the incarnation, because sponsoring them shares in their evil work (v. 11). It is a ban on supporting false teaching, not on basic kindness to unbelievers.

theology.title: Truth and love are not rivals
theology.body: "Truth" appears five times in the first four verses, always alongside love. God is never love without truth or truth without love; the Word came "full of grace and truth" (John 1:14; Psalm 85:10). John's love is the reason he warns, and his truth aims at keeping a church safe.

theology.title: No Father without the Son
theology.body: Whoever remains in Christ's teaching "has both the Father and the Son" (v. 9). No one can honor the Father while rejecting the Son as He truly is (John 5:23; 14:6). Who Jesus is, fully God and truly human, is not a side issue; it decides whether a person knows God at all.

theology.title: Blessing from Father and Son
theology.body: The greeting promises grace, mercy and peace from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Father's Son (v. 3). Placing the Son beside the Father as the source of divine blessing is a quiet confession of His deity. The command John repeats, love one another, is the one heard "from the beginning" (v. 5; Leviticus 19:18).

application.title: Kindness is not endorsement
application.body: John never tells believers to be rude to people who disagree. He tells them not to host, fund or promote teaching that denies Christ (verses 10–11). Today sharing, subscribing and donating are all forms of partnership.
application.question: What are you amplifying with your clicks or money that you would not want to be a partner in?

application.title: Beware the advanced version
application.body: Every generation has teachers offering a more enlightened faith that has moved past the old creeds. John calls that running ahead, and it ends in losing God. Growth means going deeper into Christ, not past Him.
application.question: Is there an idea you embraced mainly because it felt more sophisticated than what you were taught?

application.title: Some things need a face
application.body: John had much more to say but chose to wait and speak face to face (verse 12). Correction and comfort are often too important for a text thread. Joy, he says, is completed in person.
application.question: Which hard conversation are you trying to handle by message that really needs to happen in person?
